  \caption{\textbf{Nine arms on identical folds.} All arms are fitted and scored on the SAME 3 leave-one-combination-out folds of one synthetic benchmark instance ($d=6$, $k=7$, ground-truth interaction rank 2), each fold repeated over 3 seeds, under one shared protocol (800 optimisation steps, batch 128, lr 0.003, 16 integration steps, Adam) and one shared coupling (entropic unbalanced Sinkhorn, $\varepsilon=0.05$, 25 iterations). nED is normalised energy distance, ED(pred, post)/ED(pre, post), so 1.0 is the no-change predictor; the absolute distance and the denominator are given alongside because the ratio hides the scale. Lower is better. \textbf{Grp} is a compact letter display over adjacent paired tests: arms sharing a letter were NOT statistically separated and must not be read as ranked. $^{\ddagger}$ marks arms whose 95\% CI crosses the no-change line. $^{\dagger}$ DeepSetsEndpoint is trained on the paired displacement rather than the shared coupling: it has no integration step, so it would apply the coupling's barycentric projection directly as a map (measured 2.14$\times$ displacement inflation, scoring worse than no change on its own training conditions). The exception is documented rather than hidden. \textbf{Power.} IHC-FM (full) beats FactoredAdditiveCFM by +2.350 normalised ED (paired CI excludes zero, margin clears the 0.25 threshold) over 3 folds. The within-model ablation (main effects only vs full) is better powered, because both arms share fold, seed and schedule: paired difference +0.000 nED, 95\% CI [-0.015, +0.014], which includes zero (1/3 folds, sign test $p=1$). Case-study columns are pooled normalised ED read back from the organoid LOCO screen and the chronological purged finance split; only three arms were run on real data, and the remaining cells are marked \texttt{--} (not evaluated) rather than back-filled. Parameter counts are matched to IHC-FM's allocation (22,103) by solving each neural baseline's width.}
